page: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processor operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, supporting hyperthreading with two threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. System memory measures 21.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, allocating 2.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware flags include AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. The configuration does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage, and provides a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier compute capabilities alongside standard memory bandwidth. The processor records a Geekbench single-core score of 1167.0 and a multi-core score of 4460.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 8394.73. Multi-threaded stress-ng throughput reaches 7392.44, whereas single-core stress-ng performance falls into the lower quartile at 1405.39. Memory testing shows 49.97 GB/sec during uncached 256 MB reads and 37.19 GB/sec on sequential writes. For specific workloads, clang compilation scores 6955.0, static web throughput reaches 6.37 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput measures 7.25 million operations per second. Lower-tier performance appears in PassMark physics and large language model inference, where 7B parameter prompt processing registers at 12.14 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the c5n.2xlarge is its specialized ratio of elevated 10 Gbps networking relative to core count, paired with a non-standard memory capacity of 21.0 GB. Without local NVMe volumes, disk I/O depends entirely on external network block storage. Given these specifications and benchmark results, the instance fits network-intensive computational tasks, CI/CD compilation jobs, in-memory caching nodes, static web serving tiers, and distributed data processing pipelines that require reliable network throughput.
